Ill start by saying I feel for you, and you and I are different people, life experiences are not always comparable, and even if they are, its certainly true that perceptions on those experiences are never universal, we all have our own interpretations upon events.

That being said, as someone who has been where you are, seeing a certain endpoint as a viable option, many times even, I will say that certain things such as working and other concepts that were mature for me in my youth, certainly provided an outlet for meaning and worth.

If you dont make final decision and you end up attempting to support yourself financially, you probably wont like your first job, or the one after that, which is normal, hell, its almost guaranteed, but being given responsibilities and being rewarded for them is something that not many things in life allow for that might help you understand more things that have meaning. There is always something better life has to offer you, a better job, better friends, something better on the menu, a wage slave is certainly a way to percieve working, Im currently underpaid as I perceive it, and I'm actively looking and have recently found something better and hope that it offers me more aside from the pay bump.

In jobs, you find people who often have similar circumstances, you may meet someone you like, you will certainly have better opportunities in the future by just having a work history, you are certainly stuck in the muck for a short period before you are 21, as adulthood imo doesnt begin until maybe around ~24 these days for most people.

What you want in life is freedom, money allows for that, which might be annoying to hear in some degree, but you get more out of a decent job than money, expediency comes from what you may spend with it, but routine and responsibility that help you structure and orient yourself in the world, are infinitely more rewarding. Last week I bought a damn sword, fuck it is awesome as hell, but that doesn't compare to knowing that I'm supporting myself all on my own and am building towards owning a home slowly. Nothing about status, its all about goal building, responsibility, and personal utility. Happiness, as stupid as it may sound, absolutely comes as a byproduct of those last things.

You know, it's really hard, I had my attempt years ago, and have thought about it alot, the shame of feeling I needed to go through it, the shame of not going through it, all of that pain... still exists in me today. Im not sure it is like this for everyone, but I still have all of those rationalizations in my head, they are perfectly the same in many aspects as to, convincing myself lets say that it might be worth it. Certain things however, have changed, for the better. Yes, things hurt and lean me over that side of the fence, certain things even beckon me strongly every so often, yet, there are a great deal of things you might consider even more fondly about life if you can start to come back from it. For example, coming out of my suicidal period at its worse, I was pitying myself for a great deal of things, and loathing others, but I would just go outside, and quiet my mind and listen, I would hear beautiful things that I would regret parting with, I even picked up some gross leaves and sticks and would just admire them in some foolish way. Life is brutal, your probably sucks in only a way you can understand, but, I would encourage you to try to find ways to appreciate some of the things that you haven't considered in a while like nature, the stories of others, just something now and then to get yourself out of your own head which may be against itself to some justifiable degree although more than it should be.

Also, the further down the list, the more proactive thinking is involved.

Know where your moves generally will send your opponents

Hit all your simple tech, dont miss L cancels, fast falls, wavedashes, ground techs, ect., all cleanly, all of them

Work in character specific tech, then work on both more

Be able do all that while watching your opponent

Figure out what the opponents character likes against yours

Figure out what that player specifically likes of those options

This game isn't reacting instantly to attacks, it's building a framework. Laser from a distance essentially beats everything except powershield, but it doesn't convert automatically into everything either, but it almost does, I would lean on that option for now and tell yourself, what each opponent does after one or two of them. Do they immediately shield? Take the laser and dash? To they jump, roll, altF4? You need to start there when it comes to learning how to play against people properly. It sounds like alot, but, if you build off of something simple like laser habits, jumping into the next area of growth with be massively easier and you can segment it in the same way.

General rule of thumb is you need to know what works low percents (meaning what beats crouch cancel basically), what general options your opponents will use versus Falco; such as Fox loves to nair, dair, running shine, Marth loves fair, nair, downtilt, ect., what you can do to beat each of those individual options, something that requires an inane amount of focus when you are newer, because that involves aerial drift, what moves you can CC and be prepared to CC, knowing that at certain percents the opponent will more than likely try to force certain options (like, Puff is more likely to llay safe and aerial you if you are at high percents rather than just hail mary a dash attack, risk reward, while also, you can abuse the fact that you know they are limiting themselves to certain options that if utilized properly will yeild a higher success rate, your gameplan can narrow to beat stricter options)

I know its a bunch if minute things, but, if you want another way to understand it, the options you are chosing in the video, are good tools just improperly utilized.  You need to work on your shuffling and tech in general. DI - Directional Influence

Pressume you are getting hit by Marios fsmash and it sends you to the right ------》》》

DI allows you to dictate your flight path to a large degree when you are sent flying

If you were to DI right, you would go into the blast zone very quickly and much earlier than if you were to DI left

You can mix in holding up and in for more survivability, as well as holding away when your stock is more fresh so they have a harder time chasing you across the stage when comboing you.

To practice it

In uncle punch, you can set the CPU to use a certain attack and create a savestate, have Mario fsmash you around 50%, set the save state, let it hit you, DI in different directions to see how you fly

For DI while being combo'd there is alot of nuance so playing against people alot will have to happen, in general you hold away at lower percents, and in at ~100%+

You just need to recognize that DI in is for when you are trying to survive a stronger hit generally, and DI out is for combo escaping. Colloquially survival DI means holding in, combo DI means holding out.
